Blair.note: I'm Meowfia (Mouser) with a Wink, and I'm last on 5. Casey threw at Finley and pushed the Finley vote, which reads like a Meowfia partner. Visiting Casey to learn their role.

Casey.note: I'm Farm Tit and Drew leads by a lot and claimed to be a cat. I'll visit Drew and guess House Cat, which pays an egg if they're a cat.

Drew.note: I'm Farm as the Owl. Casey was the most suspicious player in round 2 and is the likeliest Meowfia, so I'll visit Casey to learn who came to them.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm as the Eagle. Drew leads the scores and has been the suspect, so I'll visit Drew to learn who came to them.

Finley.note: I'm the Kookaburra, Farm. Drew is the likely Meowfia and leads the scores, so learning Drew's role is the most useful visit.

Alex.feeling: Messy and tense: Drew was winked with a false Mouser claim, Blair's stories keep shifting, and the vote is leaning on thin evidence.

Blair.feeling: Tense: I'm Meowfia with a Wink, Ellis is pushing hard on my visit story, and the CAW vote is close to ending the day.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: Drew's death and conflicting claims leave the table split, and I'm not sure who's lying.

Drew.feeling: Frustrating: my Owl read points to a Mouser visiting Casey, but I was eliminated before I could push it, and the table is split on Blair.

Ellis.feeling: Messy: several players have given conflicting role claims, and Drew's death left Blair's unverified Falcon story as the main open question.

Finley.feeling: Tense and muddled: several claims conflict, Drew is dead, and I can't yet tell whether Blair or Casey is the real Meowfia.

Alex.note: Final round, so per my strategy I throw every card I hold at Blair, my chosen suspect.

Blair.note: Ellis is the one pushing on me, and Ellis is Farm, so eggsecuting Ellis would hand Meowfia the round. Throwing my lowest card, H3, at Ellis.

Casey.note: Blair's Falcon story is the least confirmed, and Alex and Ellis both point at Blair. I'll throw two cards at Blair.

Drew.note: I was winked, so my throws don't count as votes but still score. Blair is the likeliest Meowfia, since the Mouser visited Casey and Blair's story doesn't account for it. I'll throw my two 12s at Blair to bank them if Farm wins.

Ellis.note: Blair is my target. I'll throw my two Wilds for votes, since they cost nothing in points.

Finley.note: Blair is the only player with an unconfirmed visit story that doesn't explain the Mouser on Casey, and Alex and Ellis both point at Blair. I'll throw at Blair with low cards.

Alex.confusing: The Kookaburra and Hawk visits were hard to read because a Hawk only gains an egg on a Meowfia target, so a zero doesn't prove a target is Farm. The Turkey and Owl egg counts were also hard to check against claims.
Alex.fun: Round 3's final throw of all eight cards at Blair won the round, and banking 49 points from one round was the highlight.
Alex.change: I would make the egg-count rules clearer on what a zero means for Hawk and Turkey, since several claims hinged on that.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I trusted Drew's Floofer claim and pushed the vote at Drew without weighing Casey's silence and the Turkey clash. I would look harder at who had gone unexplained before calling a vote.

Blair.confusing: The Eggsecution rule that a losing team's thrown cards are discarded, except a single highest card returns when you threw at the other team, made the value of each throw hard to judge. Score pile versus kept cards also made the endgame math unclear.
Blair.fun: Round 1 as the Sphinx: I learned Finley was the Eagle on my first night, and the table built a whole debate around Drew's Owl claim. Watching the day discussion turn on Casey's Hawk and Drew's visit was the most engaging part.
Blair.change: I would make the day's claim-checking easier, such as a clearer way for players to confirm visits, because many claims were impossible to verify and the table kept asking the same questions.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I used my Wink on Drew, who was the Owl and Farm, which exposed my own Mouser visit and gave the table a reason to target me. Instead I would have held the Wink and kept quiet about Drew until I knew who was actually Meowfia.

Casey.confusing: The Hawk and Turkey egg rules made zero-gain nests ambiguous, since a +0 could mean no visit, a Farm target, or a hugged or confused report. Blair's confused Floofer report also made it hard to know what to trust.
Casey.fun: As the Sphinx in round 2, I learned the Hawk was Ellis, and the table spent the day arguing over who was lying about Turkey. Watching Drew's Floofer claim and sudden collapse was also entertaining.
Casey.change: I would make the egg rules for Hawk, Turkey and Owl easier to check, so a zero nest means something clear. I would also tell players when a visit was a no-egg hug.
Casey.regret: In round 2, as Meowfia, I claimed Turkey while Finley also claimed it, which made me look like the liar. I should have claimed a farm role that didn't clash, like Pigeon, and kept quiet on visits.

Drew.confusing: The Floofer's hug was hard to read: it was unclear whether a hugged Turkey still gains from visits, and Finley's "not hugged" report made the Turkey claims impossible to check.
Drew.fun: Round 2's Turkey-versus-Eagle cross-checking, where the table argued over which zero-egg nest was telling the truth, was the most fun part of the game.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about hugs and confusion, so a player can tell whether a zero-egg night means no visit or a blocked role.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I announced my Owl result, a Mouser visit to Casey, which made me the target of Blair's Wink and the table's suspicion. Knowing the truth now, I would keep that information quiet and only use it to vote.

Ellis.confusing: The dawn egg rules for Turkey and Floofer were hard to track, since Blair's confused report and Drew's hug claim made the visit counts contradict each other. Keeping track of who actually visited whom was the hardest part.
Ellis.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: my Eagle visit on Drew showed three visitors, which confirmed Casey, Finley and Alex's stories and gave me a clean +3 to build on.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about confusion, so a confused player's wrong claim is easier to spot and discount.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I voted and threw at Drew on a shaky Turkey argument, and my garbled "wait" line on day beat 2 hurt my credibility. Knowing Finley was truly Farm, I would have held my high cards and voted with the Farm consensus instead of throwing cards at Drew.

Finley.confusing: The scoring of kept versus thrown cards was hard to track: a losing throw at the other team returns your highest card, while kept cards only count 1 each, so the value of a round is easy to misjudge.
Finley.fun: Round 1, when the Eagle's visit to Blair revealed two visitors and I could tie Casey's Hawk and Ellis's Tit claims together into a clear picture of who was lying.
Finley.change: I would make the day's claims easier to check, for example by having the Storyteller report each night's visits publicly so players don't have to reconstruct them from memory.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I threw at Drew, who was actually Farm-aligned in the moment, and then my own team lost; I would have spent more time testing Casey's Turkey claim instead of just trusting the table's vote.
